newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss National Bank cuts discount rate to 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss National Bank cuts discount rate to 1.0 pct.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said it was lowering its discount rate by 50 basis points to 1.0 percent, effective Friday, September 27.
The central bank said in a statement that the move was in line with the recent decline in Swiss money market rates.
The discount rate was last cut, by 50 basis points, on December 14.

A central bank spokesman said the bank decided to cut the discount rate as a means of underscoring the recent decline in money market rates. "The (rate cut) move is more a reassurance to the market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," SNB spokesman Werner Abegg said.
The discount rate was last cut to one percent in February 1978, and was subsequently raised to 2.0 percent in November 1979.

The SNB pointed out in its statement that it had been supplying the money market with additional liquidity since the beginning of August "in order to prevent monetary strain" and as a result, some money market rates fell below the discount rate.
"By lowering the discount rate, the Swiss National Bank underlines its expectation that the interest rate decline will continue for some time," it added.
